newsitem.title: USA: Bevy of foreign crudes beckon U.S. Gulf refiners.
newsitem.headline: Bevy of foreign crudes beckon U.S. Gulf refiners.

text.p: A bevy of foreign crudes beckoned U.S. Gulf Coast refiners on Wednesday as May buying began to wind down, traders said.
Traders were still awaiting word late Wednesday on likely foreign crude deliveries into the NYMEX after the May contract expired on Tuesday.

Some two million barrels of Nigerian Bonny Light and North Sea Brent were widely expected to be delivered, although last-minute Exhange for Physical (EFP) transactions might have allowed sellers to avert delivery, traders said.

Unless the NYMEX receives specific requests for crudes other than the benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing, the alternative grades would be alloted in 80,000 barrel parcels beginning with the longest positions, traders said.
Trade sources said that a foreign crude has not been delivered into the NYMEX in at least five years, but this could not be immediately confirmed.
Physical delivery of foreign crude on NYMEX contracts is a rare event as it is usually uneconomic and is considered the option of last resort, traders said.
If a company receives Brent instead of WTI, it would receive a fixed discount of 30 cents per barrel to compensate for the differing crude qualities.
Bonny Light would require the company to pay a premium of 60 cents per barrel.
Separately, a U.S. privately held company was offering at least one cargo of Brent into the Gulf Coast for around May 15-20 arrival, asking about WTI minus 75-80 cents a barrel, traders said.
A U.S. major was reselling a Brent cargo for May 6-8, asking around 70-75 cents under WTI delivered, traders said.
The spread between WTI and Brent was around $1.60-65 a barrel Wednesday afternoon, narrower from Tuesday but still wide enough to encourage transatlantic trade.
Two Oseberg cargoes were still looking for homes for mid-May delivery, with the asking price around WTI minus 70 cents a barrel.
From West Africa, a trading house was showing at least two cargoes of Qua Iboe for May 15-25 delivery, asking dated Brent plus $1.85 a barrel.
In Latin America, an equity producer was still offering a Cusiana cargo for May 15-17 delivery. The last Cusiana cargo was sold around WTI minus $1.57 a barrel on a delivered basis.
Elsewhere, Bolivia's state oil company sold 260,000 barrels of reconstituted crude oil to a U.S. trading company for loading around May 7-10, trade sources said.
Yacimientos Petroliferos Fiscales Bolivianos (YPFB) sold the crude at a discount of $5.95 a barrel to benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
YPFB held the tender on its own behalf, as well as in the name of equity producers YPF, Perez Companc, Tesoro and Ultramar/Diamond Shamrock.
The tender marked YPFB's second attempt to sell the crude. An earlier tender, which called for loading April 15, was canceled and reissued after the company received only one bid.
YPFB received two offers in the new tender.
Bolivia's reconstituted crude is mixed with gasoline to raise its API gravity to 45 degrees.
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
